summary: lifecycle-interceptions S0 foundation store (cinatra#2038, epic #2037) — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL (lifecycleInterceptionsSchemaQueries) co-located in the already route-reachable src/lib/artifacts/artifact-review-gate-schema.ts and spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries in the SAME PR. FOUNDATION SLICE — no consumers ship here; every schema/contract later slices (S1–S7b) depend on is landed here, fenced. Nine brand-new tables plus additive gate-store extensions plus one compiled-config column. lifecycle_policy_rules: the org-scoped policy LATTICE bounds (required/forbidden) per (checkpoint, artifact type, destination class, origin kind) — the ABSENCE of a row IS 'silent' (unconstrained) and is never stored; a UNIQUE (org, checkpoint, type, dest, origin) key anchors the lookup. artifact_produced_outbox: the transactional ArtifactProduced event with a DETERMINISTIC event_id PK (sha256 of the gate key artifact_id+representation_revision_id+event_kind) so a same-tx re-emit under replay is idempotent, an enumerated emitter CHECK (createSemanticArtifact | dashboard_twin_writer | object_cms_snapshot_capture), continuation mode/address, and a (artifact, revision, kind) UNIQUE so the deterministic id and the tuple agree; the reconciliation sweeper looks for the exact deterministic id, detecting a suppressed emit. lifecycle_continuation_park: checkpointed-mode park records (evaluate-then-park) carrying the policy-decision id, the protected effect, a reevaluation intent, and a TTL that ALWAYS resumes into a terminal policy_unresolved block on the protected effect. gate_advisory_comments: the zero-authority advisory seam — gate-bound (FK artifact_review_gates ON DELETE CASCADE), provenance-stamped (author id/kind + timestamp + optional run causation), idempotent per (gate, idempotency_key), and STRUCTURALLY DECISION-FREE (no decision/disposition columns exist; rows live WITH the gate). artifact_verification_records (DECIDED SCHEMA S4): {reviewedTarget, repairedTarget} + scope manifest + field/visual before/after. run_selected_skill_revisions (DECIDED SCHEMA S3): the immutable per-run pinned skill-revision set (UNIQUE per run+skill; distinct from telemetry-only agent_run_skills_used, untouched). cms_snapshot_targets (DECIDED SCHEMA S5): the locally pinned CMS snapshot target + scope manifest + apply binding {connector_instance, resource_type/id, base_remote_revision_ref, operation_id} (UNIQUE operation_id). gate_suggestion_snapshots + suggestion_decision_ledger (DECIDED SCHEMA S4 auditor re-home): gate-bound immutable suggestion snapshots + the decision-application ledger. GATE-STORE EXTENSIONS (additive ALTERs on the #1796 review-gate tables): artifact_review_gates.expires_at (TTL) + reopen_count (lineage attempt counter); artifact_review_resume_outbox.max_attempts + dead_lettered_at (the dead-letter STATE marker, NULL = live) + last_error, with a partial dead-letter index — the resume drain dead-letters an exhausted intent instead of re-leasing it forever (ops-surfaced). agent_templates.lifecycle_config (JSON-as-text) carries the compiled agent-manifest lifecycle declarations trigger-style (mirrors trigger_mode / gated_steps). NO foreign keys to agent_runs ON PURPOSE (the review-gate precedent): rows keyed by run/gate ids validated at write time, outliving run-row churn; the advisory/verification/suggestion rows FK to artifact_review_gates(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (meaningless without their gate), the ledger FKs the snapshot. ADDITIVE + IDEMPOTENT — DDL MIRRORS the bootstrap leaf exactly (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS): a no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install, executed by db migrate on an existing deployment; unqualified names ride the runner's search_path (the app schema). down() drops the nine fresh tables (children before parents) and the added columns/indexes (loses lifecycle rows by design; empty on a fresh install; nothing consumes them at S0). SEQ 0079 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on origin/main (core__0077, from the merged #1986 assistant-pause set) AND the in-flight open PR #2049's claimed core__0078; a concurrent lane may land the next seq first, in which case a rename-only renumber is normal (FLAGGED for the coordinator's train). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
